projects.title: libr
projects.summary: A moderated, censorship-resilient social network framework.
projects.description: A moderated, censorship-resilient social network framework. Posts are stored on a replicated Kademlia DHT for partial immutability and are published only after a majority quorum of moderators approves them. Core services in Go with Docker, PostgreSQL and cryptographic certificates for tamper-evident storage, with a React web client. A week-long public beta drew 250+ landing-page visitors, 570+ page views, 100+ downloads and 1,000+ user posts.
projects.problem: Centralised platforms can remove content at will, while fully decentralised networks have no way to keep harmful content out. libr aims for a public forum that resists censorship and is still moderated.
approach: Three roles: clients, database nodes and moderators.
Posts are stored on a replicated Kademlia DHT for partial immutability, which is cheaper and faster than writing every message to a blockchain.

A post is stored only after more than half of the community’s moderators sign it. A moderation certificate carries their signatures, so any node can check it, and no single moderator decides a post’s fate.

The co-authored paper models this as Byzantine fault-tolerant voting: with m moderators, up to ⌊(m − 1)/2⌋ faulty ones can neither block nor force a decision. It also proves safety, liveness and censorship resistance.
Core services are written in Go with Docker and PostgreSQL; cryptographic certificates make stored content tamper-evident.
Users run a desktop client with a Go backend and a TypeScript UI, distributed through a Windows installer and an APT repository.

projects.title: Mini-K8ts
projects.summary: A lightweight container orchestrator for edge environments.
projects.description: Lightweight container orchestrator for edge environments: <50 MB control-plane RAM, 25 MB binary, <1s startup, PostgreSQL as ACID state store. Reliability-aware multi-stage scheduler sustains 220+ tasks/sec (97.8-100% efficiency, 1000 tasks in 4.2s, 2000 in 9.1s). Heartbeat self-healing marks failed nodes down in 4s and requeues orphaned tasks within 2s; a horizontal job autoscaler, token RBAC, rate limiting, optional mTLS, Postgres-backed leader election and Prometheus/Grafana monitoring.
projects.context: Course project, Virtualization and Cloud Computing
projects.problem: Edge devices often have 512 MB to 4 GB of RAM and unreliable links, while a standard Kubernetes control plane assumes data-centre resources. Mini-K8ts keeps orchestration, scheduling and self-healing inside a small footprint.
approach: A REST API server and a multi-stage scheduler (filter, score, bind) with shadow resource tracking, so it never over-commits a node between heartbeats.
Reliability-aware placement: nodes earn a reliability score from their heartbeat and task history, and high-priority tasks go to reliable nodes.
Workers register and send heartbeats with live CPU and memory every 2 seconds. A node is marked down after two missed heartbeats, and its orphaned tasks are requeued with exponential backoff.
PostgreSQL is the ACID state store, with lease-based leader election across scheduler replicas. A horizontal job autoscaler scales on pending-queue depth and cluster CPU.
Token RBAC, rate limiting, optional mTLS, Prometheus metrics with Grafana, and the m8s CLI.

projects.title: FileNest
projects.summary: Semantic, multi-modal search over decentralized storage, with no central index.
projects.description: Mentored a hierarchical distributed tagging system that combines semantic embeddings with Kademlia DHT P2P routing for multi-modal search across text, PDFs, images and video. BERT, Sentence-Transformers and CLIP pipeline designed to target 15-20 files/sec indexing and sub-100ms queries; built during Summer RAID 2025 at IIT Jodhpur.
projects.role: Mentor, then co-author of the design paper
projects.context: Summer RAID 2025, then research at IIT Jodhpur
projects.problem: Content-addressed storage such as IPFS lets any peer serve a file, but finding content still depends on search services run by a single operator, who can filter, delist or reorder results. FileNest spreads the index itself across peers and finds content by meaning, not by an identifier the user must already know.
approach: Files stay in the storage layer. FileNest indexes only each file’s content identifier, its embedding and the peer that offered it.
Embeddings are organised into a hierarchy of tagging vectors: routing points in embedding space, created as content arrives, under similarity thresholds that tighten with depth.

A Kademlia DHT assigns each tagging vector to a peer by hashing its value at creation. Similarity decides which region an embedding belongs to; the DHT decides where that region’s state lives, so no peer holds a whole subtree.
A query descends the same hierarchy. Each tagging vector keeps a covering radius, and a subtree is skipped only when the triangle inequality proves it holds no match, so pruning never drops a result.
Text, images, PDFs and video share one embedding space (Sentence-Transformers and CLIP in the RAID build).

projects.title: GitCury
projects.summary: A command-line tool that writes commit messages with AI and batches git work across many repositories.
projects.description: Git workflow automation that cut commit time from 17 minutes to 32 seconds (97% faster) across 298 files in a 4 MB footprint. Semantic file clustering reduces API calls by 90% (3.2x faster); 3 clustering strategies, concurrent worker pool, shipped via Homebrew, Scoop, Docker and 6 OS/arch binaries.
projects.problem: Committing across many repositories means writing many messages and repeating the same git steps. GitCury automates both.
approach: A Go CLI built on Cobra that generates commit messages with the Gemini API.
Batch operations commit, push and write messages across all configured repositories at once, using a pool of workers.
Related changes are grouped before generation, by directory, by file pattern or by semantic embedding, so one request covers a whole group.
Distributed through Homebrew, Scoop, Docker and prebuilt binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows.
